content.title: Giants vs. Yankees recap: Logan Webb struggles in 7-0 Opening Night loss
content.text: Giants Opening SeriesLive Blog EndedMar 25, 2026 NBC Universal, Inc. On “Giants Talk,” Tony Vitello joins Alex Pavlovic and Bonta Hill to discuss leaving Tennessee for his new MLB managerial job with San Francisco. What to KnowThe San Francisco Giants opened the 2026 MLB season with a 7-0 loss to the New York Yankees on Wednesday night at Oracle Park under new manager Tony Vitello.Giants ace Logan Webb was tagged with the defeat in his fifth consecutive season-opening start, allowing six earned runs on nine hits over five innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.San Francisco mustered just three hits during the loss, and Yankees starter Max Fried was stellar across 6 1/3 innings with zero runs, two hits, one walk and four strikeouts.Yankees superstar slugger Aaron Judge struck out three times against Webb and ended the night 0-for-5 with four total K's. Read below for all the game highlights, news, analysis and postgame press conferences from Oracle Park in San Francisco: Tony Vitello, Logan Webb, Matt Chapman, and Luis Arraez speak to reporters following San Francisco's Opening Night loss to the New York Yankees on Wednesday at Oracle Park. Giants infielder Luis Arráez speaks to reporters after San Francisco’s 7-0 Opening Day loss to the New York Yankees on Wednesday at Oracle Park. SAN FRANCISCO -- In one respect, Tony Vitello, who managed his first big league game on Wednesday, is very similar to all of the Giants fans who watched on Netflix. Vitello has been wildly successful in his chosen profession, but he said this spring that when it comes to keeping up with his favorite shows on streaming services, he's reliant on family members. He doesn't have many subscriptions of his own. "I just steal passwords from my family," he said. Vitello didn't need one to watch Wednesday's season opener, and he probably won't need to log in for a rewatch. His debut in the big leagues was a game the Giants would rather forget. SAN FRANCISCO – Every single Giants fan at Oracle Park rose out of their seats to cheer before the first pitch of Wednesday’s game against the New York Yankees was even thrown. That is the effect of Logan Webb, who was given a standing ovation during pregame introductions on MLB Opening Night. The momentum carried over into the first inning, as Webb struck out the first two batters he faced – including Aaron Judge – before Cody Bellinger flied out to left to end the inning in a 1-2-3 punch. San Francisco’s offense failed to capitalize on continuing the momentum, and despite having a runner on first and third with one out, the game remained scoreless heading into the second inning. Logan Webb's Opening Night didn't go how he wanted, but he joined a Giants legend in the process in San Francisco's 7-0 loss. Logan Webb was 2nd Giants pitcher to allow 7+ runs on opening day since the team moved to San Francisco in 1958. Gaylord Perry also allowed 7 vs Astros in 1970— Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) March 26, 2026 There is a silver lining, though -- Perry finished that season second in Cy Young voting and led the league in wins, games started and innings pitched. Maybe Webb will do the same? Giants manager Tony Vitello speaks to reporters ahead of San Francisco’s Opening Day matchup against the New York Yankees on Wednesday at Oracle Park. BOX SCORE SAN FRANCISCO -- Tony Vitello and his new staff got together on Wednesday morning to go over some final details before their season opener. A couple of hours later, the new Giants manager sat at a podium and smiled as he recalled the big plate of pastries that had been placed in the room. "I avoided one of those pastries and they all looked pretty deadly," Vitello said. "So, I'm at least 1-0 today." By the end of the day, Vitello and the Giants were 0-1 where it mattered. Read Full Article The Yankees couldn't have asked for anything better from ace Max Fried to open their 2026 season. The left-hander exited tonight's game with a 7-0 lead and quote the stat line: 6 1/3 innings, two hits, zero runs, one walk and four strikeouts. Jazz Chisholm has made plenty of good plays during his career, but the Yankees infielder surprised even himself with this one. Aaron Judge will be wearing a Golden Sombrero when he leaves Oracle Park tonight. After striking out three times against Giants starter Logan Webb, things didn't get any better when Judge faced reliever Keaton Winn in the top of the sixth inning when he was caught looking for the second out of the frame. Luckily for Judge, his Opening Night struggles haven't stopped the Yankees from holding a commanding lead. Logan Webb's first start of the 2026 season spiraled quickly and ended after five rough innings. Webb allowed nine hits, seven runs (six earned) and one walk while striking out seven Yankees batters. The Giants' ace left the game with San Francisco trailing 7-0, and right-handed pitcher Keaton Winn replaced him. An RBI single and a throwing error gave the Yankees two more runs off Logan Webb in the top of the fifth inning for a 7-0 lead. After surrendering back-to-back singles to Cody Bellinger and Ben Rice, Webb gave up an RBI knock to Giancarlo Stanton to make it 6-0. The Giants then had a chance to turn two on a ground ball from Jazz Chisholm, but a throwing error by Willy Adames that Casey Schmitt couldn't scoop at first base led to another Yankees run. Logan Webb gave Aaron Judge a hat trick and reached a career milestone in the top of the fourth inning. The Giants ace sent the Yankees slugger back to the bench for a third time to end the frame. And with the strikeout, Webb now has 1,000 in the seventh year of his MLB career. In the top of the fourth inning, Yankees shortstop Jose Caballero challenged Logan Webb's first pitch of the frame, believing it was a ball. But the newly implemented ABS challenge system ruled that Webb's sinker caught the strike zone, though Netflix's broadcast missed the scoreboard replay because they were interviewing Giants manager Tony Vitello. Caballero's challenge was deemed unsuccessful and he later grounded out to third base. Welcome to Oracle Park, Harrison Bader. The Gold Glove outfielder made a sliding catch in the top of the fourth inning, robbing Trent Grisham of what might have been a bloop single to shallow center field otherwise. Opening Night marks Bader's first game with San Francisco after the team signed him to a two-year contract in MLB free agency this offseason. The ballpark by the Bay is known for its shadows in the batter's box during early afternoon games, and Yankees star Jazz Chisholm admitted he couldn't see when he was struck by Logan Webb in the second inning. Jazz Chisholm on his HBP: "I'm not gonna lie to you. I couldn't see it, that's why I probably got hit. I'm normally good at getting out of the way." 🤣 pic.twitter.com/NLJXntZDTy— Rob Friedman (@PitchingNinja) March 26, 2026 It's no secret it's hard to come back from a 5-0 deficit, but this stat shows things might be nearly hopeless for the Giants with seven innings still left in the game. After spurning the Giants in free agency to stay with the Yankees following the 2022 season, it's safe to say fans in San Francisco aren't too fond of Aaron Judge. The New York superstar got an earful before eventually striking out against Logan Webb in his first at-bat of the game in the first inning. Logan Webb found himself in some trouble to start the second, and the Yankees took advantage. The Giants ace surrendered a one-out single to Giancarlo Stanton before hitting Jazz Chisholm Jr. with a 92.5-mph sinker. José Caballero then made San Francisco pay with an RBI double to score the game's first run. Then, Ryan McMahon added to the damage with a two-run single to make it 3-0. The damage didn't stop there when, one Austin Wells single later, Trent Grisham plated another pair of Yankees runs with triple into, well, Triple's Alley. Webb was able to escape the inning by striking out Aaron Judge for the second time and sending Cody Bellinger down swinging as well. The Giants had runners on first and third with one out in the bottom of the first inning, but they couldn't capitalize. After Luis Arraez led things off with a walk off Max Fried, Matt Chapman reached first on a fielder's choice when the Yankees couldn't complete a double play thanks to his speed. Rafael Devers then dropped a shallow fly ball in between center field and second base for a bloop single, with Chapman advancing to third from first. But a Willy Adames strikeout followed by a Jung Hoo Lee groundout ended the inning. Logan Webb was locked in, striking out Yankees outfielders Trent Grisham and Aaron Judge to start the 2026 season. Webb got Cody Bellinger to fly out to left to wrap up a 1-2-3 first inning. The Giants' ace needed just 17 pitches to get through the frame. All the luminaries were in attendance at Oracle Park for Wednesday's season opener. The Giants brought back former managers Bruce Bochy and Dusty Baker, and the iconic skippers christened the new season by throwing out the ceremonial first pitches. It's time for the "Main Event" -- and who better to ring it in than WWE star and San Francisco native Jey Uso. Yankees star Aaron Judge has won three AL MVP awards, but he has yet to capture a World Series title in 10 MLB seasons, leading fans to criticize him for not delivering championship No. 28 to the Bronx. Giants legend Barry Bonds was in a similar boat, having won seven NL MVP awards but never winning a World Series. During Netflix's pregame show, Bonds defended Judge against his naysayers. Spectators -- many in Netflix kayaks -- flocked to the famous body of water to take in tonight's game. Jameis Winston couldn't help but poke fun at himself outside the Crazy Crab'z booth at Oracle Park. Over a decade after the former FSU quarterback was embroiled in a crab leg theft scandal, Winston addressed the "elephant in the room" on the Netflix broadcast while discussing one of the stadiums most beloved food items. Will San Francisco gain any ground on New York tonight when it comes to their all-time Opening Day winning percentages? Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey (2006-08) and NFL quarterback Jameis Winston (2013, 14) both played baseball for the Florida State Seminoles. SAN FRANCISCO -- Jared Oliva is 30 years old and hasn't played in the big leagues since 2021, when he struggled in 40 at-bats for the Pittsburgh Pirates. He spent all of last season in Triple-A with the Milwaukee Brewers and the previous year in Double-A with the Seattle Mariners, and his recent history includes time in the Mexican Winter League. Oliva admitted Wednesday that there were times when it probably made sense to give up on this whole baseball dream. "It felt like I was going against the current," he said, smiling. For the time being, at least, the only body of water Oliva has to worry about is the one behind his new ballpark. The Giants selected him to their roster on Wednesday morning, choosing him over 24-year-old Luis Matos, a former top prospect, and a couple of left-handed options. Manager Tony Vitello lit up when talking about giving Oliva the news. President of baseball operations Buster Posey said it was a roster move that thrilled everyone "to a man" in the coaches' room and clubhouse. The Giants officially have released their 2026 MLB Opening Day roster, and one of the few standouts is veteran outfielder Jared Oliva. Oliva earns the final bench spot in an outfield headlined by Heliot Ramos, Harrison Bader and Jung Hoo Lee. Before the official roster release, Giants broadcaster Duane Kuiper shared his thoughts on what he saw from the Santa Clarita native throughout spring training. “I compared him, in a way, to Andres Torres in 2010,” Kuiper said on KNBR’s “Murph & Markus” show. SAN FRANCISCO -- After two decades, the streak finally is over. Heliot Ramos is starting in left field for Wednesday night's season-opening game against the New York Yankees, becoming the first Giant since Barry Bonds in 2006-07 to start back-to-back Opening Day games in left field. When he made the start last year, Ramos became the 19th different left fielder in 19 seasons. The Giants came one swap short of setting an MLB record. The St. Louis Browns/Baltimore Orioles also started 19 different left fielders in 19 years from 1937 to 1955. New manager Tony Vitello laughed Monday when asked if he had any tricks up his sleeve, a real possibility since the Giants optioned Bryce Eldridge to Triple-A last week and could have used Ramos in the DH spot for the first game. Vitello said he wanted things to be as normal as possible on day one of the 2026 MLB season and recalled when he heard about the streak after taking over as manager. When the Giants officially announced Tony Vitello as their new manager, San Francisco’s star pitcher Logan Webb was one of the first players to openly express his excitement for the clubhouse’s new leader. Recalling his first encounter with the former Tennessee baseball coach, Webb told NBC Sports Bay Area’s Bonta Hill and Alex Pavlovic about the first time he physically met up with Vitello after the announcement. “He called me one day,” Webb said. “I sent him a text and I said, 'Welcome to the Giants. F it. Let’s win while we’re here,' you know what I mean? He called me one day, talking about some pitching stuff, and I told him I was in Nashville, actually, for a wedding. “And I was like, 'Hey, are you here by chance?' And he was. I think he has a place on Broadway. So, he was like, 'Hey, I’ll meet you at this time at this bar.' It was hard to hear each other, but we talked for a long time, and it was a blast. That’s when I just knew the competitor that I am and he [is] the exact same.” Read Full ArticleOn Giants Talk, Alex Pavlovic and Bonta Hill sit down with San Francisco ace Logan Webb from spring training as he gets set for the 2026 MLB season. The 2025 MLB season might have been the only year that three-time Cy Young Award-winning pitcher Justin Verlander spent with the Giants, but his impact is still being felt by his former teammates. In an interview with NBC Sports Bay Area's Alex Pavlovic and Bonta Hill during spring training, Giants ace Logan Webb discussed just how much the nine-time All-Star taught him during his tenure with San Francisco. "You brought up leading the league in strikeouts, which I don't think anyone saw that coming," Webb said on "Giants Talk." "I didn't see it coming. A lot of that had to do with Justin. The way he attacks hitters, the way he's reading swings, the way he scouts, the mentality that you need to bring to do that sort of thing. That was Justin." Webb, who led the National League with 224 strikeouts, also touched on the fact that Verlander helped him grow as a pro. SAN FRANCISCO -- The biggest spring roster decision for the Giants was made a few days before they returned to Oracle Park. Top prospect Bryce Eldridge was told last week that he will start this season back in Triple-A. The rest of the puzzle came together Wednesday morning, a few hours before the Giants will open the 2026 MLB season against the New York Yankees. Veteran Jared Oliva won the final bench spot and right-handers Keaton Winn and Caleb Kilian will fill out the eight-man bullpen. Here's the entire Opening Day roster for this weekend's series: The clear a roster spot for Oliva, the Giants DFA'd young outfielder Luis Matos. The 24-year-old was out of options and had an inconsistent camp. It's likely the end of the line in orange and black for a former top prospect. The biggest competition at the end of camp was in the outfield, with several players with varying skill sets vying for the jobs behind Heliot Ramos, Harrison Bader and Jung Hoo Lee. Jerar Encarnación will be the fourth outfielder and is likely to start at designated hitter often over the first few weeks of the season. SAN FRANCISCO -- There's a good debate to be had about the magnitude of Logan Webb's start in the World Baseball Classic quarterfinals earlier this month. Given that Webb was pitching for Team USA, some have made the argument that it was the biggest start of his career. You could also very easily place it third, behind his two NLCS starts in 2021, or fourth, trailing also his Game 162 masterpiece that allowed the Giants to clinch the NL West title that year. Realistically, the conversation probably starts with the quarterfinal ranking second at best given that his Game 5 start in 2021 was a must-win game against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Regardless, it's a fun discussion to have, and it leads to two greater points. First, there's no doubt that Webb consistently rises to meet the moment. Logan Webb always is in the picture for most innings pitched at the end of the year, but wins have been another story. ESPN's David Schoenfield weighed in on what the Giants can expect from Webb entering his eighth MLB season, all with San Francisco. "It's not bold to predict that Logan Webb will lead the National League in innings pitched," Schoenfield wrote in a piece published Tuesday. "He has done that three seasons in a row." Webb barely had the edge on Garrett Crochet last season for innings pitched in the entire league with 207.1. Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey made history this offseason, hiring an incredible college baseball personality with zero big league experience as San Francisco's new manager. MLB commissioner Rob Manfred joined KNBR's "Murph & Markus" on Tuesday morning to give his opinion on the Tony Vitello hire. "I think the hiring of a college coach to be a big league manager is part of a larger evolution in the relationship between college baseball and MLB," Manfred claimed. Vitello, on Wednesday, will become the league's first manager without any prior professional experience, but his preparation isn't in question. SAN FRANCISCO -- When Tennessee athletic director John Currie called Tony Vitello in the summer of 2017 and asked him to interview for the head coaching job, Vitello didn't have much time to think. Everything was coming at him quickly, but as he packed for the interview, he figured he should be prepared for what might happen if all went well. Vitello grabbed the only orange shirt he had, a Nike golf polo he occasionally would wear on recruiting trips because it kept him cooler than some other options in his closet. Currie soon offered Vitello the job, and a day later, he sat down at a table at the airport to sign a life-altering contract. He knew exactly what to wear. "I thought, let's get this going with some orange," he recalled this spring. "And little did I know, I offended everybody in Vol nation." As the ink dried on that deal, Vitello learned a valuable lesson about pantones. SAN FRANCISCO -- This was supposed to be a night of firsts for Tony Vitello, but it ended up being more memorable for another Giant. Bryce Eldridge hit a loud opposite-field home run late in an exhibition game against Sultanes de Monterrey at Oracle Park, and the 21-year-old said it was his first time going deep in any big league ballpark. The closest he had come was his time in Sacramento -- where the Athletics play along with the River Cats -- and a few times taking BP at big league parks ahead of the 2023 draft. "That was cool. I definitely embraced it running around the bases," Eldridge said. "I was trying not to smile at all, trying to be cool, but going around third I couldn't stop myself from smiling a bit." The homer was Eldridge's second in two days since the Giants returned to California. He also homered in Sunday's exhibition in Sacramento, but he was on the other side in that game. The Giants announced last week that Eldridge will begin the season back in Triple-A. Read Full Article
